messages.subject: Multi-session data with factor covariate - level issue
parts:
Hello,

I am working on muti-session data and I am using a sex covariate (factor). There are six sessions (A, B, C, D, E and F).
I read it is necessary that the levels of a factor covariate are the same in each session, whether or not all levels are used.
This may require the levels in the final capthist object to be set manually.

I am facing this situation as only males were photo-captured in session C.
I tried to change the factor levels manually but in vain. 

You can see below what I have tried to do. If you have any guidance, it would be very appreciated.
Kind regards, 

Elsa
-------------------------------------------------------------------

Code:

> class(secr.ALL)
[1] "list"     "capthist"

When I create secr.ALL, I get the warning message:
> secr.ALL <- read.capthist(...
Warning message:
In verify.capthist(temp) :
  Levels of factor covariate(s) differ between sessions

As you can see in session C, only males were photo-captured:
> attr(secr.ALL$C, "covariates")
           V5
LEO10  m
LEO12  m
LEO13  m
LEO14  m

Attempt to change the factor levels directly:
> levels(covariates(secr.ALL)$C$V5) <- c("m","f")
> nlevels(covariates(secr.ALL)$C$V5)
[1] 1

I then tried to use an intermediate dataframe but once I bring it back in the capthist object, it goes back to one factor level:
> dataC <- covariates(secr.ALL)$C
> levels(dataC$V5) <- c("m","f")
> nlevels(dataC$V5)
[1] 2
> covariates(secr.ALL)$C <- dataC
> nlevels(covariates(secr.ALL)$C$V5)
[1] 1

parts:
Also, I worry that you may get into trouble with the order of factor levels (it's safer to keep levels in alphabetical order as this is the default). That would suggest
covariates(secr.ALL$C) <- data.frame(V5 = factor(rep('m', nrow(secr.ALL$C)), levels = c('f','m')))
(back in read.capthist you could set covnames = 'sex' instead of the mysterious 'V5' default)

Murray

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Multi-session data with factor covariate - level issue
parts:
This is a recurring problem, so I'm thinking of adding a repair function 'shareFactorLevels'  to the next release. If you're in a hurry then copy and paste from here. Usage (no example yet) is msCH <- shareFactorLevels(msCH).
Murray


shareFactorLevels <- function (object, columns = NULL) {
    if (ms(object)) {
        if (!is.null(covariates(object))) {
            df <- do.call(rbind, covariates(object))
            if (is.null(columns)) columns <- 1:ncol(df)
            for (i in columns) {
                if (is.factor(df[,i])) {
                    levelsi <- levels(df[,i])
                    for (sess in 1:length(object)) {
                        covariates(object[[sess]])[,i] <-
                            factor(covariates(object[[sess]])[,i],
                                   levels = levelsi)
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    object
}


shareFactorLevelsR Documentation

Fix Inconsistent Covariates

Description

Factor covariates can give trouble in multi-session models if the levels differ among sessions. A warning is provided by verify.capthist. This function forces factor covariates to use the same levels.

Usage

shareFactorLevels(object, columns = NULL)

Arguments

object

multi-session capthist object or list of traps or mask objects

columns

indices of columns to fix (default all)

Details

Factor-valued covariates are coerced to use the same set of levels for each session of a multi-session capthist object or each component of a list of traps or masks. The combined level set is the union of all levels in separate sessions. The order of levels follows the default in factor (alphabetical).

Value

An object of the same class as input.

See Also

verify.capthist
